318	            Logger.warn(`[BackupManager] Backup already loaded with id ${backup.id} - ignoring`)
319	          } else {
320	            this.backups.push(backup)
321	          }
322	
323	          Logger.debug(`[BackupManager] Backup found "${backup.id}"`)
324	          await zip.close()
325	        }
326	      }
327	      Logger.info(`[BackupManager] ${this.backups.length} Backups Found`)
328	    } catch (error) {
329	      Logger.error('[BackupManager] Failed to load backups', error)
330	    }
331	  }
332	
333	  async runBackup() {
334	    // Check if Metadata Path is inside Config Path (otherwise there will be an infinite loop as the archiver tries to zip itself)
335	    Logger.info(`[BackupManager] Running Backup`)
336	    const newBackup = new Backup()
337	    newBackup.setData(this.backupPath)
338	
339	    await fs.ensureDir(this.AuthorsMetadataPath)
340	
341	    // Create backup sqlite file
342	    const sqliteBackupPath = await this.backupSqliteDb(newBackup).catch((error) => {
343	      Logger.error(`[BackupManager] Failed to backup sqlite db`, error)
344	      const errorMsg = error?.message || error || 'Unknown Error'
345	      NotificationManager.onBackupFailed(errorMsg)
346	      return false
347	    })
348	
349	    if (!sqliteBackupPath) {
350	      return false
351	    }
352	
353	    // Zip sqlite file, /metadata/items, and /metadata/authors folders
354	    const zipResult = await this.zipBackup(sqliteBackupPath, newBackup).catch((error) => {
355	      Logger.error(`[BackupManager] Backup Failed ${error}`)
356	      const errorMsg = error?.message || error || 'Unknown Error'
357	      NotificationManager.onBackupFailed(errorMsg)
358	      return false
359	    })
360	
361	    // Remove sqlite backup
362	    await fs.remove(sqliteBackupPath)
363	
364	    if (!zipResult) return false
365	
366	    Logger.info(`[BackupManager] Backup successful ${newBackup.id}`)
367	
368	    newBackup.fileSize = await getFileSize(newBackup.fullPath)
369	
370	    const existingIndex = this.backups.findIndex((b) => b.id === newBackup.id)
371	    if (existingIndex >= 0) {
372	      this.backups.splice(existingIndex, 1, newBackup)
373	    } else {
374	      this.backups.push(newBackup)
375	    }
376	
377	    // Check remove oldest backup
378	    const removeOldest = this.backups.length > this.backupsToKeep
379	    if (removeOldest) {
380	      this.backups.sort((a, b) => a.createdAt - b.createdAt)
381	
382	      const oldBackup = this.backups.shift()
383	      Logger.debug(`[BackupManager] Removing old backup ${oldBackup.id}`)
384	      this.removeBackup(oldBackup)
385	    }
386	
387	    // Notification for backup successfully completed
388	    NotificationManager.onBackupCompleted(newBackup, this.backups.length, removeOldest)
389	
390	    return true
391	  }
392	
393	  async removeBackup(backup) {
394	    try {
395	      Logger.debug(`[BackupManager] Removing Backup "${backup.fullPath}"`)
396	      await fs.remove(backup.fullPath)
397	      this.backups = this.backups.filter((b) => b.id !== backup.id)
398	      Logger.info(`[BackupManager] Backup "${backup.id}" Removed`)
399	    } catch (error) {
400	      Logger.error(`[BackupManager] Failed to remove backup`, error)
401	    }
402	  }
403	
404	  /**
405	   * @see https://github.com/TryGhost/node-sqlite3/pull/1116
406	   * @param {Backup} backup
407	   */
408	  backupSqliteDb(backup) {
409	    const db = new sqlite3.Database(Database.dbPath)
410	    const dbFilePath = Path.join(global.ConfigPath, `absdatabase.${backup.id}.sqlite`)
411	    return new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => {
412	      const backup = db.backup(dbFilePath)
413	      backup.step(-1)
414	      backup.finish()
415	
416	      // Max time ~2 mins
417	      for (let i = 0; i < 240; i++) {
418	        if (backup.completed) {
419	          return resolve(dbFilePath)
420	        } else if (backup.failed) {
421	          return reject(backup.message || 'Unknown failure reason')
422	        }
423	        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 500))
424	      }
425	
426	      Logger.error(`[BackupManager] Backup sqlite timed out`)
427	      reject('Backup timed out')
428	    })
429	  }
430	
431	  zipBackup(sqliteBackupPath, backup) {
432	    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
433	      // create a file to stream archive data to
434	      const output = fs.createWriteStream(backup.fullPath)
435	      const archive = archiver('zip', {
436	        zlib: { level: 9 } // Sets the compression level.
437	      })
438	
439	      // listen for all archive data to be written
440	      // 'close' event is fired only when a file descriptor is involved
441	      output.on('close', () => {
442	        Logger.info('[BackupManager]', archive.pointer() + ' total bytes')
443	        resolve(true)
444	      })
445	
446	      // This event is fired when the data source is drained no matter what was the data source.
447	      // It is not part of this library but rather from the NodeJS Stream API.
448	      // @see: https://nodejs.org/api/stream.html#stream_event_end
449	      output.on('end', () => {
450	        Logger.debug('Data has been drained')
451	      })
452	
453	      output.on('finish', () => {
454	        Logger.debug('Write Stream Finished')
455	      })
456	
457	      output.on('error', (err) => {
458	        Logger.debug('Write Stream Error', err)
459	        reject(err)
460	      })
461	
462	      // good practice to catch warnings (ie stat failures and other non-blocking errors)
463	      archive.on('warning', function (err) {
464	        if (err.code === 'ENOENT') {
465	          // log warning
466	          Logger.warn(`[BackupManager] Archiver warning: ${err.message}`)
467	        } else {
468	          // throw error
469	          Logger.error(`[BackupManager] Archiver error: ${err.message}`)
470	          // throw err
471	          reject(err)
472	        }
473	      })
474	      archive.on('error', function (err) {
475	        Logger.error(`[BackupManager] Archiver error: ${err.message}`)
476	        reject(err)
477	      })
478	      archive.on('progress', ({ fs: fsobj }) => {
479	        if (this.maxBackupSize !== Infinity) {
480	          const maxBackupSizeInBytes = this.maxBackupSize * 1000 * 1000 * 1000
481	          if (fsobj.processedBytes > maxBackupSizeInBytes) {
482	            Logger.error(`[BackupManager] Archiver is too large - aborting to prevent endless loop, Bytes Processed: ${fsobj.processedBytes}`)
483	            archive.abort()
484	            setTimeout(() => {
485	              this.removeBackup(backup)
486	              output.destroy('Backup too large') // Promise is reject in write stream error evt
487	            }, 500)
488	          }
489	        }
490	      })
491	
492	      // pipe archive data to the file
493	      archive.pipe(output)
494	
495	      archive.file(sqliteBackupPath, { name: 'absdatabase.sqlite' })
496	      archive.directory(this.ItemsMetadataPath, 'metadata-items')
497	      archive.directory(this.AuthorsMetadataPath, 'metadata-authors')
498	
499	      archive.append(backup.detailsString, { name: 'details' })
500	
501	      archive.finalize()
502	    })
503	  }
504	}
505	module.exports = BackupManager

# Set 2 bug log (not fixed)

Line numbers are those of the original JavaScript files at HEAD.

1. server/managers/CoverSearchManager.js:67 - `onError(error.message)` passes one argument, but the callback that SocketAuthority.js:415 supplies is `(provider, errorMessage)`: the message is emitted as `provider` and `error` is undefined in the `cover_search_provider_error` event.
2. server/managers/CoverSearchManager.js:227-235 - after `if (typeof result === 'string') covers.push(result)` there is no `else`, so `.covers` and `.cover` are also read on a string result (harmless: both are undefined).
3. server/managers/MigrationManager.js:17 - the default `configPath = global.configPath` reads a global that is never set (the server sets `global.ConfigPath`, capital C), so the default is always undefined and the constructor throws "Config path is required" unless the caller passes configPath (Database.js does).
4. server/managers/CoverManager.js:25-32 - `getFilesInDirectory` returns `fs.readdir(dir)` without await inside try/catch, so the catch never sees a rejected readdir; the rejection reaches the caller (`removeOldCovers`) instead of the `[]` fallback.
5. server/managers/CoverManager.js:34-44 - `removeFile` has the same pattern: the promise chain is returned inside try/catch without await, so a failing `fs.unlink` rejects to the caller and the `return false` fallback is dead code.
6. server/managers/CoverManager.js:50 - `imageExtensions` contains '.jiff', which is not an image extension (probably meant '.jfif'), so an old `cover.jfif` is never removed.
7. server/managers/CacheManager.js:65-70 and 171-176 - the `stream.pipeline` callback calls `res.sendStatus(500)` on a response that `ps.pipe(res)` may already have started to send (possible ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT on a read error).
8. server/managers/BinaryManager.js:157 - `assets?.bin?.[this.platformSuffix]?.[assetName]` indexes with `this.platformSuffix`, which is null on an unsupported platform (getPlatformSuffix() returns null at line 149): the lookup key becomes the string 'null' and the error says "platform null". ## 10. CLAUDE.md / brief: wrong, unclear or missing

- **Boundary casts at typed modules.** Rule 5 allows a boundary cast at an "untyped module". Three of my casts are at typed modules whose types lack a member that exists at runtime (`Sequelize.QueryTypes`, `Module._nodeModulePaths`, `module._compile`). I used the same `x as typeof x & {...}` form and counted them as "other". Please rule.
- **libs/fsExtra return types.** CLAUDE.md names only its missing methods. Its `remove` and `copy` also have the inferred return type `Promise<any> | undefined` (and `move`, per the probe), so `.catch` or `.then` on them is TS2532. I used `(fs.remove(x) as Promise<void>)`.
- **MigrationManager `!` count.** It has 18 (F 12, L 6), all on init-then-use fields or validated names. Say if that count is acceptable.
- **CoverSearchManager string result.** A string search result is typed `string & { covers?: undefined; cover?: undefined }`, because the code reads `.covers` and `.cover` on strings too (bug 2). This is an annotation, not a cast.
- **Seeing the compiled output.** The no-emit check cannot show what a file compiles to. A private emit into the scratch folder (`--noEmit false --noEmitOnError false --outDir <scratch>`) did, and would be worth adding to the brief.
- **Middleware-set properties.** The rule "a property that a middleware sets is required in the consumer's type" has no answer for a manager that a converted controller calls with the optional type (BackupManager.uploadBackup, section 2).
- **Report file.** The brief asks for setN/report.md, but the harness refuses a sub-agent's Write of a report file.
- **Scratch folder.** set2/ also holds my check artefacts: base-src, base-out, emit, the logs and thisprobe.ts.
